mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% monthly for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which typically precedes restrictive monetary policy and higher input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE falls below 3.5% for four consecutive months in a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for six consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines by more than 1% monthly for six consecutive months.
